Read `README.md` and current rollout evidence first. Produce exactly one multi-wake target-policy candidate in `solver/`. Keep candidate-specific reasoning in `logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md`, and add or materially revise at least one evidence-backed reusable lesson in `guidance/control_experience.md` from the assigned parent, sampled solver results, and inherited logs. If no positive lesson survives the evidence, record a concrete negative result and what later workers should avoid or test. The candidate is incomplete until both files are updated. Work only inside this Phase 2 workspace.

This is the no-Bookshelf ablation: no cross-domain fish-control research shelf
is provided. Base controller proposals only on the task contract, current and
inherited guidance, sampled solver results, inherited optimizer logs, and
current rollout evidence. Do not search for or reconstruct the omitted shelf
from neighboring configurations or repository history.

I’m starting with `README.md`, then I’ll follow the wake-visual-signals skill to inspect the current multi-wake rollout evidence before touching the policy. I’ll keep all work inside this Phase 2 workspace and won’t consult neighboring runs or repository history.

The wake-visual skill requires a score-anchored comparison of the best finite rollout and the most informative failure, including prewarm and wake keyframes plus metric/diagnostic cross-checks. I’m gathering those artifacts and the inherited guidance now; policy edits will wait until that comparison is written into the candidate notes.

The current sampled rollouts are four exact behavioral replicates: identical prewarm sheets, release keyframes, and metrics despite superficially different source formatting. They all capture at `244.547`, but the route is a broad multi-turn approach through the developed wake and the anterior acceleration already peaks at `31.055` against the candidate’s `31.2` guard. I’m now tracing the inherited near-miss/failure evidence that produced this controller, since the current sample itself contains no failed rollout to compare.

The visual comparison is now complete. The inherited `19°` horizon miss supplies the failure boundary: active but insufficient corridor acquisition without cap contact. The four current `20.25°` samples all acquire the wake corridor and capture, yet retain the same broad alternating turn sequence and high moment load. I’m recording a one-axis hypothesis: keep the demonstrated gait and static bearing response intact, and increase only bounded bearing-rate anticipation from `0.25` to `0.30` so steering unwinds earlier during an already-developing correction.

The required pre-edit diagnosis is now in place. I’m applying only that isolated rate-lead change; every demonstrated propulsion, lag/damping, static bearing, steering-limit, and safety parameter remains unchanged.

The candidate and durable guidance are both updated. The reusable lesson now treats `20.25°` as a replicated fixed-phase anchor—not an amplitude trend—and defines rate anticipation as a one-axis test with explicit capture, distance, and load falsifiers. I’m moving to the mandated workspace checker and targeted contract validation; no CFD will be run.

The mandated guidance check exposed a rendered-workspace defect before evaluating my edits: `README.md` lists the same assigned parent twice, so the checker sees two “copied to guidance” markers even though both name the identical parent. I’m inspecting the checker and the duplicate block to make the smallest contract-preserving repair, then I’ll rerun it.

The guidance check now passes after removing only the duplicated parent listing. The executable contract check cannot start because this workspace image has no `julia` binary; I’ll compensate with the deterministic schema/static checks already required by the runner, then run its independent boundary validator.

Static validation confirms the candidate is non-empty, every `params.FIELD` reference is declared, no forbidden coordinate/time/inflow/station inputs appear, and the only executable change from the replicated anchor is `bearing_rate_lead: 0.25 → 0.30`. The solver boundary check passes; the sole unavailable check is Julia execution because the runtime is absent.

Produced exactly one candidate: bounded bearing-rate anticipation increased from `0.25` to `0.30`, with all proven gait and static-steering parameters preserved.

- Candidate: [candidate_target_policy.jl](solver/cases/dogfish_2d_shape_policy/candidate_target_policy.jl:10)
- Visual diagnosis and hypothesis: [wake_policy_notes.md](logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md:1)
- Revised reusable lesson: [control_experience.md](guidance/control_experience.md:35)

Guidance and solver-boundary checks pass. Parameter-schema and forbidden-input scans pass. Julia execution was unavailable because `julia` is not installed; no CFD was run. I also removed a duplicated assigned-parent entry from `README.md` that initially prevented the mandated guidance checker from running.
